name: Astaxanthin

lead: Astaxanthin is a red-pink xanthophyll carotenoid made by microalgae such as Haematococcus pluvialis and responsible for the colour of salmon, shrimp and flamingos. It is sold as a dietary supplement, typically derived from algae.

In looksmaxxing and skincare it is used for skin hydration, elasticity and defence against UV damage. Systematic reviews find modest improvements in moisture and elasticity in small trials, with less consistent effects on wrinkles.

paras: Astaxanthin is a potent lipid-soluble antioxidant that spans cell membranes and quenches reactive oxygen species, and in cell studies it dampens UV-induced inflammatory signalling and collagen-degrading enzymes. Whether these effects translate into meaningful clinical change depends on the trials, which are mostly short.

Supplements are generally well tolerated at studied doses, with occasional mild gastrointestinal effects and, at high intake, a reddish skin tint. Safety in pregnancy and long-term use is not well established. Most trials are small, many are industry-funded, and several enrolled mainly healthy Japanese women, limiting how far results generalise.
